 China's Tax Authority Issues Reminder Ahead of Offshore Trust Tax Filing Deadline
 Oct 22, 2026
      Hubbis

 -->
 China's State Taxation Administration (STA) has reminded taxpayers with offshore trusts to review their arrangements and declare and pay individual income tax before 22 October 2026 to benefit from relief from late-payment surcharges during a 90-day transitional period, according to a Xinhua report carried by 21st Century Business Herald (21世纪经济报道). The STA published the reminder on its website on 19 October. 
 The reminder relates to the Announcement on Individual Income Tax Matters Concerning Offshore Trusts, issued by the Ministry of Finance (MOF) and the STA on 24 July 2026. Under the announcement, taxpayers subject to the rules must declare and pay individual income tax on offshore trust income. Those who complete declaration and payment within the transitional period will not be charged late-payment surcharges, according to the report. The STA said tax authorities would provide guidance and filing services to help taxpayers meet their obligations and protect their rights.
 According to an analysis by China Briefing, published by Dezan Shira & Associates, the rules provide for a 20 percent individual income tax on certain gains and income arising at different stages of an offshore trust's lifecycle, including the transfer of assets into a trust, income generated during its operation, certain distributions and termination. Some provisions apply retrospectively to 1 January 2023.
 Reuters reported on 16 October, citing three people familiar with the matter, that the STA had instructed staff to pursue individuals potentially liable for offshore trust taxes, using information including the Hurun wealth rankings and corporate filings. Wealth advisers and lawyers told Reuters that some wealthy individuals were winding down offshore trusts and selling shares to raise cash ahead of the deadline.
 **
 Source · China Briefing · Reuters via The Standard 
 WRITTEN BY
 Mark Nelligan
 Fund Manager at Lombard
 Odier
